newsitem.title: USA: OUTBOARD MARINE BOOSTED BY RIVAL BID.
newsitem.headline: OUTBOARD MARINE BOOSTED BY RIVAL BID.

text.p: Outboard Marine Corp shares rose nine percent Monday, after a tender offer of $18 a share was made by an affiliate of Greenway Partners, an investment group which owns about 9.9 percent of the company's outstanding shares.
The bid is $2 a share higher than a $16 a share offer announced by Detroit Diesel Corp on July 9.

But one analyst thought the tender offer Thursday by Greenmarine Holdings, the affiliate of Greenway that counts Soros Fund Management LLC as an investor, might have been made in the hope that Detroit Diesel would raise its bid in response.

"My feeling is that they probably figured the $16 offer by Detroit Diesel was a little bit low," said Michael Pizzi, an analyst who follows the Waukegan, Illinois-based outboard motor and boat maker for Standard & Poor's Equity Group.
But he was also skeptical that a much higher bid would be made for Outboard Marine.

"They've been having troubles operationally," Pizzi said. They've had losses in recent periods and it's going to take some time to turn around ..., so I can't see a bidding war developing for the company."
The company reported a net loss of $21.6 million, or $1.07 a share, for the fiscal 1997 first six months, ending March 31.

But an investor with deep pockets and time to allow the company to turn around could make the company more valuable in the long run, said James Schmitt, an analyst and investor at Westcountry Financial.
"This company is worth a lot more than 18 a share," he said.
Detroit Diesel would not comment on the Greenmarine bid Friday.
Outboard Marine shares were up 1-8/16 at 17-13/16 Friday.
